h: Chocolate country on the south side
p: Lifford Lane sits in the south of Birmingham, near Kings Norton and Stirchley, and that puts AirHop within easy reach of one of the city's best-loved family attractions. Cadbury World is in Bournville, just up the road, with exhibits on how chocolate is made, interactive zones and a few treats along the way. Pair the two and you've got a day of bouncing and chocolate, which is about as close to a child's dream as it gets. Book both ahead, especially in the holidays.

Bournville itself is worth a wander. The model village was built by the Cadbury family for their workers, and its leafy streets, village green and Selly Manor Museum, a pair of timber-framed buildings moved here and rebuilt, give a real sense of history. Stirchley, nearby, has a growing reputation for independent cafes, bakeries and craft beer bars, if the grown-ups fancy a treat.

For fresh air, the Rea Valley Route follows the River Rea through south Birmingham, and the towpaths of the Worcester and Birmingham Canal run close by. The Lickey Hills Country Park, on the south-western edge of the city, has woodland walks and viewpoints over the countryside, perfect after an indoor session. Kings Norton Park has play areas and open space if you'd rather stay closer. A tip for the session itself: the mixed-reality games are popular, so it's worth heading over to them early before queues build up. Have a plan for drinks and snacks too, because a session of bouncing works up a proper appetite, and the Stirchley cafes are only a few minutes away.
